$note: Deploy manifest — EXAMPLE. Copy to `deploy-targets.json` (gitignored) or let
`npm run init` write it for you.
One entry per live deployment you are responsible for. `npm run deploy:all`
reads it and, for each target: cross-checks the account against your wrangler
config, checks for unapplied D1 migrations, deploys, then fetches the URLs in
WHY THE ACCOUNT ID IS DUPLICATED. It appears here and again in your wrangler
config, and the deploy script refuses to run if the two disagree. That
disagreement is the whole point: it is what turns 'deployed to the wrong
Cloudflare account' from a silent success into a loud failure. Editing one
file without the other should hurt.
NO SECRET VALUES LIVE HERE, in this file or in yours. The `credentials`
block records only WHERE a secret is registered and WHAT it is called —
never a value. Worker secrets are set out-of-band with `wrangler secret put`,
which prompts for them; nothing in this repo reads, prints or transmits one.
An account id is an identifier rather than a credential — it appears in
dashboard URLs — but this file is gitignored anyway, because a manifest of
your live deployments is nobody else's business.

targets.label: My blyg
targets.account_label: Which account this is, in words — read at deploy time to confirm

credentials.registry: wherever you keep track of your own secrets
credentials.note: Names, not values. AI_PROVIDER_KEY is optional — it powers [TK] generation and nothing else; a blyg without one works fully.
